title: Understanding Earth Through Maps
subject: Social Science
description: Explore how maps help us understand our world — from basic map elements and political/physical/thematic maps to cartographers, historical maps, and modern GPS, Satellite, and GIS maps.

questions.question: What is a map?
options: A drawing that represents a place and its features
A photograph taken only by satellites
A written story about a country
questions.explanation: A map is a drawing that represents a place, showing its features using symbols, titles, and other elements.

questions.question: What does the Title of a map tell you?
options: The exact population of the area
The names of everyone who made the map
questions.explanation: The Title tells you what the map is about, helping you understand its purpose at a glance.

questions.question: What is a Legend (or Map Key) used for?
options: Explaining what the symbols on a map mean
Showing the exact temperature of a place
Listing famous people from the area
Measuring how old the map is
questions.explanation: A Legend, or Map Key, explains what each symbol used on the map represents.

questions.question: What does a Compass Rose show on a map?
options: Directions like North, South, East, and West
The number of roads in a city
questions.explanation: A Compass Rose shows directions — North, South, East, and West — helping you orient yourself on the map.

questions.question: What four directions does a compass rose typically show?
questions.explanation: A compass rose typically shows the four main directions: North, South, East, and West.

questions.question: What does the Scale on a map help you understand?
options: Real-world distance compared to the map's distance
The exact colour of the land
The names of all towns shown
questions.explanation: The Scale helps you understand how the distance shown on the map relates to real-world distance.

questions.question: Why is the scale important when reading a map?
options: It lets you calculate real distances between places on the map
It tells you the map's title
It shows which direction is North
questions.explanation: The scale lets you calculate the actual real-world distance between two places shown on the map.

questions.question: Select ALL of the four basic map elements described in the chapter.
questions.explanation: The four basic map elements are Title, Legend, Compass Rose, and Scale. A password is not a map element.

questions.question: A map's legend explains what the symbols on the map mean.
questions.explanation: The legend (or map key) explains what each symbol on the map represents.

questions.question: If you want to know what a small tree symbol means on a map, which part of the map would you check?
questions.explanation: The Legend explains the meaning of symbols like a small tree icon used on the map.

questions.question: In the Oakwood Town map example, which of these was shown as a symbol in the legend?
questions.explanation: The Oakwood Town map example included symbols for places like Town Hall, School, Park, River, Road, and Railway.

questions.question: Why do maps use symbols instead of drawing every detail realistically?
options: Symbols make maps clear and easy to read without clutter
Symbols are required by law for all maps
Realistic drawings are impossible to create
Symbols make maps more colourful only
questions.explanation: Using symbols keeps maps clear and easy to read, rather than being cluttered with overly realistic details.

questions.question: Without a legend, it can be hard to understand what symbols on a map mean.
questions.explanation: Without a legend, the meaning of symbols used on a map would be unclear to the reader.

questions.question: If a map has no title, what problem could this cause?
options: Readers might not understand the map's overall purpose
The map would automatically become inaccurate
The compass rose would stop working
questions.explanation: Without a title, readers may not immediately understand what the map is meant to show.

questions.question: Which map element helps you figure out which direction is North?
questions.explanation: The Compass Rose helps you determine directions, including North, on a map.

questions.question: If North is at the top of a map (as shown by the compass rose), which direction is usually at the bottom?
options: There is no direction at the bottom
questions.explanation: If North is at the top, South is usually shown at the bottom of the map.

questions.question: If East is shown to the right on a map, which direction is usually shown to the left?
questions.explanation: If East is to the right, West is usually shown to the left of the map.

questions.question: Which map element would help you calculate the real-world distance between two towns shown on a map?
questions.explanation: The Scale helps you calculate real-world distances between places shown on a map.

questions.question: A map's scale shows that 1 cm equals 1 km. If two towns are 5 cm apart on the map, how far apart are they in real life?
questions.explanation: Since 1 cm = 1 km, 5 cm on the map equals 5 km in real life.

questions.question: A map's scale shows that 1 cm equals 2 km. If two towns are 3 cm apart on the map, how far apart are they in real life?
questions.explanation: Since 1 cm = 2 km, 3 cm on the map equals 6 km in real life.

questions.question: Which of the four map elements tells you what the entire map is about?
questions.explanation: The Title tells you the overall subject or purpose of the map.

questions.question: A compass rose only shows the direction North and nothing else.
questions.explanation: A compass rose shows all four main directions — North, South, East, and West — not just North.

questions.question: In the Oakwood Town map, why might a river be shown using a wavy blue line symbol in the legend?
options: Symbols represent real features in a simple, recognisable way
Rivers cannot be shown on maps
questions.explanation: Symbols like a wavy blue line represent real features, such as rivers, in a simple, easy-to-recognise way.

questions.question: In a town map's legend, which symbol category would 'Road' most likely fall under?
questions.explanation: Roads are shown as transportation/infrastructure symbols in a town map's legend.

questions.question: Why does a map need BOTH a legend and a compass rose, not just one of them?
options: A legend explains symbols, while a compass rose explains direction — both are needed to fully understand a map
A legend and compass rose show the exact same information
Only a legend is ever needed on any map
Only a compass rose is ever needed on any map
questions.explanation: A legend explains what symbols mean, while a compass rose explains direction — together they help you fully understand and use a map.

questions.question: Which map element would you use to find out how far one place is from another?
questions.explanation: The Scale helps you determine real-world distance between places on a map.

questions.question: Which map element would help you find your way if you were walking north through Oakwood Town?
questions.explanation: The Compass Rose shows direction, helping you know which way is north as you walk.

questions.question: A map's scale always shows real-world distances at exactly the same size as they are drawn on paper.
questions.explanation: Maps use a smaller scale ratio (like 1 cm = 1 km) rather than showing real-world size directly on paper.

questions.question: Why is a railway line typically shown using a distinct symbol on a town map's legend?
options: So it can be told apart from roads and other features easily
Because railways are not allowed on maps
Because railways are always shown in red only
Because railways never appear near towns
questions.explanation: A distinct symbol helps readers easily tell a railway line apart from roads and other map features.

questions.question: What could happen if a map-maker forgot to include a legend?
options: Readers might not understand what the symbols on the map mean
The map would automatically show the wrong location
The compass rose would stop working correctly
questions.explanation: Without a legend, readers would have difficulty understanding what the map's symbols represent.

questions.question: Which two map elements work together to help you understand BOTH direction and distance at the same time?
questions.explanation: The Compass Rose helps with direction, while the Scale helps with distance — together they help you navigate a map.

questions.question: Besides showing distances, symbols and direction, what overall purpose do all map elements serve?
options: They help readers understand and use the map correctly
They make maps more expensive to print
They are purely decorative and serve no function
They only matter for satellite maps
questions.explanation: All map elements — Title, Legend, Compass Rose, and Scale — work together to help readers understand and use a map correctly.

questions.question: According to the chapter, a title, legend, compass rose, and scale are all essential elements of a complete, useful map.
questions.explanation: The chapter presents Title, Legend, Compass Rose, and Scale as the essential elements of a complete map.

questions.question: In the Oakwood Town map example, which map element would tell you the town has a Park?
questions.explanation: The Legend lists symbols for features like a Park, Town Hall, or School shown on the map.

questions.question: If you see an 'N' with an arrow pointing upward on a map, which map element are you looking at?
questions.explanation: An 'N' with an arrow pointing up is part of the Compass Rose, showing where North is.

questions.question: What does a Political map show?
questions.explanation: A political map shows countries, states, cities, and boundaries.

questions.question: What does a Physical map show?
questions.explanation: A physical map shows landforms such as mountains, rivers, and plains.

questions.question: What does a Thematic map focus on?
options: One specific topic, like rainfall or population
questions.explanation: A thematic map focuses on one specific topic, such as rainfall or population.

questions.question: Which map would best show the boundaries between two states?
questions.explanation: A political map is best for showing boundaries between states or countries.

questions.question: Which map would best help hikers plan a safe route through mountains?
questions.explanation: A physical map shows landforms like mountains and rivers, helping hikers plan safe routes.

questions.question: Which map would best show rainfall patterns across different areas?
questions.explanation: A thematic map focuses on one topic, like rainfall, making it best for showing rainfall patterns.

questions.question: Political maps typically show mountains, rivers, and deserts as their main focus.
questions.explanation: Political maps focus on boundaries, countries, states, and cities — not landforms like mountains or deserts.

questions.question: Which type of map is being described: 'shows countries, states, and important cities'?
questions.explanation: This description matches a political map, which shows countries, states, and cities.

questions.question: Which type of map is being described: 'shows mountains, rivers, and plains'?
questions.explanation: This description matches a physical map, which shows landforms like mountains, rivers, and plains.

questions.question: Which type of map is being described: 'focuses on one specific topic, like population'?
questions.explanation: This description matches a thematic map, which focuses on a single topic like population.

questions.question: A teacher wants students to learn how India is divided into states and union territories. Which type of map should be used?
questions.explanation: A political map shows how a country is divided into states and union territories.

questions.question: A group of students is studying forest areas and wildlife in different parts of India. Which type of map should they use?
questions.explanation: A thematic map focused on forests and wildlife would be most useful for this study.

questions.question: During a flood, rescue teams need to understand the land and river paths quickly. Which map type helps most?
questions.explanation: A physical map shows landforms and rivers, helping rescue teams understand the land and water paths during a flood.

questions.question: Farmers use political maps to understand soil and water conditions in their fields.
questions.explanation: Farmers would use thematic or physical maps to understand soil, water, and land features — not political maps, which show boundaries.

questions.question: Aarav wants to know which states share a common border with his state. Which map should he use?
questions.explanation: A political map shows state boundaries, helping Aarav find which states share a border with his.

questions.question: Meera is planning a trek and wants to know about mountains and rivers in the area. Which map should she use?
questions.explanation: A physical map shows mountains and rivers, which is exactly what Meera needs for planning her trek.

questions.question: Which map shows countries, states, and cities?
questions.explanation: A political map shows countries, states, and cities.

questions.question: A map showing mountains, rivers, and plains is a:
questions.explanation: A map showing landforms like mountains, rivers, and plains is a physical map.

questions.question: Which map would best show rainfall in different areas?
questions.explanation: A thematic map, which focuses on one topic, would best show rainfall in different areas.

questions.question: Select ALL examples of what a thematic map could show.
questions.explanation: Rainfall, population, and forests are all examples of single-topic subjects a thematic map could show. Showing only country borders describes a political map, not a thematic map.

questions.question: Why might the same place look completely different depending on which map type you use?
options: Each map type highlights a different kind of information about the same place
Places physically change shape depending on the map
Only one map type is ever accurate
Maps of the same place are always identical
questions.explanation: Different map types (political, physical, thematic) highlight different kinds of information, so the same place can look very different.

questions.question: What is one reason maps are compared to 'storybooks' in the chapter?
options: Each type of map tells a different story about a place
Maps are printed on the same paper as storybooks
Maps and storybooks both use only words
Maps have no connection to storybooks
questions.explanation: Just like different storybooks tell different stories, each type of map tells a different 'story' about the same place.

questions.question: Why do maps use symbols instead of drawing everything realistically, according to the chapter?
options: Drawing everything realistically would make maps too messy to read
Symbols are cheaper to print than realistic drawings
Realistic drawings are against the law
Symbols look more colourful than drawings
questions.explanation: The chapter explains that drawing everything realistically would make maps too messy, so symbols are used instead.

questions.question: What can a thematic map show that we cannot easily see with our own eyes, like rainfall or population?
options: Data and patterns that aren't visible just by looking at the land
The exact height of every building
The names of everyone living in a region
questions.explanation: A thematic map can show invisible data, like rainfall amounts or population density, that we can't see just by looking at the land.

questions.question: According to the chapter, why does every map 'have a purpose'?
options: Because no map can show everything about a place at once
Because maps are randomly drawn without any plan
Because all maps are political maps in disguise
Because maps never actually help anyone
questions.explanation: Since no map can show everything at once, each map is made with a specific purpose in mind.

questions.question: No single map can show everything about a place at once.
questions.explanation: The chapter explains that every map is made for a purpose, and no single map shows everything about a place.

questions.question: Which type of map would be LEAST useful for understanding how many people live in a city (population density)?
questions.explanation: A physical map focuses on landforms, not population data, making it least useful for understanding population density.

questions.question: Which type of map focuses specifically on one topic rather than showing many types of information?
questions.explanation: A thematic map focuses on just one topic, unlike political or physical maps which show broader categories of information.

questions.question: A city planner wants to see which state a particular city belongs to. Which map should they check?
questions.explanation: A political map shows state boundaries and which cities belong to which state.

questions.question: An explorer wants to know if there's a mountain range blocking their path. Which map should they check?
questions.explanation: A physical map shows landforms like mountain ranges, helping the explorer plan their route.

questions.question: A scientist studying population growth across regions of a country needs which type of map?
questions.explanation: A thematic map focused on population would best help a scientist study population growth across regions.

questions.question: A physical map's main focus is showing political boundaries between countries.
questions.explanation: A physical map's main focus is landforms like mountains and rivers, not political boundaries — that's what a political map is for.

questions.question: Which map type would be best to study forest areas and wildlife in different parts of India?
questions.explanation: A thematic map focused on forests/wildlife would be the best choice for this kind of study.

questions.question: Thematic maps can be used to study things like rainfall, population, or forests.
questions.explanation: Thematic maps focus on single topics like rainfall, population, or forests.

questions.question: Why would a thematic map showing forest cover be more useful to a wildlife researcher than a political map?
options: It directly shows the specific information (forest cover) the researcher needs, rather than just boundaries
Political maps are always more detailed than thematic maps
Thematic maps cannot show forests at all
Wildlife researchers never use any type of map
questions.explanation: A thematic map showing forest cover gives the researcher exactly the specific information they need, unlike a political map which only shows boundaries.

questions.question: Which map focuses on man-made boundaries, like state and country borders?
questions.explanation: A political map focuses on man-made boundaries, such as state and country borders.

questions.question: Which map focuses on natural landforms and features of the Earth?
questions.explanation: A physical map focuses on natural landforms, such as mountains, rivers, and plains.

questions.question: If two maps of the same country show completely different information — one shows rainfall, the other shows mountain ranges — what types of maps are these most likely to be?
options: A thematic map and a physical map
questions.explanation: A rainfall map is a type of thematic map, while a mountain range map is a physical map — so these would likely be a thematic map and a physical map.

questions.question: Why is a physical map particularly useful during natural disasters, like floods?
options: It helps rescuers quickly understand land and river paths
It shows the exact population of every village
It only shows country borders, which floods do not cross
It shows currency exchange rates for aid supplies
questions.explanation: A physical map shows land and river paths, which is essential information for rescue teams during floods.

questions.question: Give one feature typically found on a political map.
questions.explanation: Political maps typically show state and country boundaries.

questions.question: Give one feature typically found on a physical map.
questions.explanation: Physical maps typically show mountains, rivers, and other landforms.

questions.question: Why is a thematic map useful for studying rainfall or forests?
options: It focuses on just that one topic and shows it clearly across an area
It shows every possible topic at once
It never includes any useful data
It only works for studying oceans
questions.explanation: A thematic map's focus on a single topic makes it especially clear and useful for studying things like rainfall or forests.

questions.question: Why do we need different types of maps to understand the Earth?
options: Each map type highlights different information that together gives a fuller picture
Only one type of map is ever useful
Different map types show identical information
Maps are only useful for finding treasure
questions.explanation: Different map types (political, physical, thematic) each highlight different kinds of information, together giving us a fuller picture of the Earth.

questions.question: Which type of map might overlap in purpose with BOTH a physical AND a thematic map, if it shows forest cover as a type of land feature?
options: A map that combines physical land features with a thematic forest-cover focus
questions.explanation: A map focused on forest cover blends physical land-feature information with a thematic single-topic focus.

questions.question: A political map, a physical map, and a thematic map of the exact same country would all look exactly the same.
questions.explanation: Each map type highlights different information, so a political, physical, and thematic map of the same country would look quite different.

questions.question: A farmer wants to know if it will rain this week to plan planting. Which kind of map would help most?
questions.explanation: A weather-focused thematic map would help the farmer plan planting based on expected rainfall.

questions.question: A family is planning a road trip and wants to see the fastest route. Which kind of map would help most?
options: A political map showing only borders
questions.explanation: A GPS or road map would help the family find roads, routes, and the fastest way to their destination.

questions.question: In a classroom, a large world map on the wall mainly helps students learn about?
questions.explanation: A large classroom world map (a political map) mainly helps students learn about countries and their locations.

questions.question: A hiker wants to know exactly how steep a mountain trail will be before starting. Which map should they use?
questions.explanation: A physical map shows landforms like mountains, helping the hiker understand the trail's steepness.

questions.question: Why might a pilot use a completely different type of map than a hiker, even for the same region?
options: A pilot needs air routes and altitude info, while a hiker needs ground terrain details
Pilots and hikers always need the exact same information
Hikers cannot use any type of map
questions.explanation: A pilot needs information relevant to flying (like air routes and altitude), while a hiker needs ground terrain details — so they use different map types.

questions.question: Which map type would help you plan the safest route to avoid rivers or flooded areas during travel?
questions.explanation: A physical map shows rivers and landforms, helping you plan a route that avoids flooded areas.

questions.question: Different professions, such as farmers, pilots, and hikers, may use different types of maps depending on their needs.
questions.explanation: Different professions need different information, so they use different types of maps suited to their specific needs.

questions.question: Which map would be most useful for understanding how India is divided for administrative purposes?
questions.explanation: A political map shows administrative divisions like states and union territories.

questions.question: Which map would help you understand where forests and deserts are located across a country?
questions.explanation: Physical or thematic maps can show natural features like forests and deserts.

questions.question: Why is it important to choose the RIGHT type of map for a specific task?
options: The wrong map type may not show the information you actually need
All maps show exactly the same information regardless of type
Choosing a map type has no real effect on usefulness
Only political maps are ever useful for any task
questions.explanation: Choosing the right map type ensures you get the specific information you need for your task.

questions.question: Which map type would show you both natural landforms as well as their names, like the Himalayas or a major river?
questions.explanation: A physical map shows and names natural landforms such as mountain ranges and rivers.

questions.question: Which map would you use to plan a trip between multiple states or cities?
questions.explanation: A political or road map would help you plan travel between multiple states or cities.

questions.question: If you wanted to see how many people live in villages vs. cities across a region, which map would be most useful?
questions.explanation: A thematic map focused on population would show how many people live in villages versus cities.

questions.question: Which map would environmental scientists likely use most to track deforestation over time?
questions.explanation: A thematic map focused on forests/vegetation would help scientists track deforestation over time.

questions.question: A rescue team during a flood needs the land and river paths quickly. Which map type helps most, and why?
options: A physical map, because it shows landforms and rivers clearly
A political map, because it shows city names
A GPS traffic map, because it shows traffic colours
A currency map, because it shows money values
questions.explanation: A physical map clearly shows landforms and rivers, which rescue teams need to navigate quickly during a flood.

questions.question: Why do maps 'help us understand nature and people at the same time'?
options: Because different maps show both natural features and human activity
Because all maps only show natural features
Because all maps only show human activity
Because maps cannot show either nature or people
questions.explanation: Different types of maps (physical for nature, thematic/political for people) together help us understand both nature and human activity.

questions.question: Give one example of a map used for a weather-related purpose.
options: A rainfall or weather thematic map
questions.explanation: A rainfall or weather thematic map is used specifically for weather-related purposes.

questions.question: Give one example of a map used for a travel or journey-related purpose.
options: A road map or GPS map
questions.explanation: A road map or GPS map is used specifically for travel and journey-related purposes.

questions.question: Which of these would NOT typically appear as the main focus of a basic political map?
questions.explanation: Mountains and landforms are shown on physical maps, not as the main focus of political maps.

questions.question: Which of these would NOT typically appear as the main focus of a basic physical map?
questions.explanation: Country borders are the main focus of political maps, not physical maps, which focus on landforms.

questions.question: Which of these would NOT typically be the main focus of a thematic rainfall map?
options: City names shown in bold as the main focus
Areas of heavy vs light rain
questions.explanation: A thematic rainfall map's main focus is rainfall data, not city names as the primary feature.

questions.question: A group of students is studying forest areas and wildlife in different parts of India. Based on the worksheet scenario, which type of map should they use?
questions.explanation: A thematic map focused on forests/wildlife matches this scenario from the chapter's worksheet.

questions.question: A teacher wants students to learn how India is divided into states and union territories. Based on the worksheet scenario, which type of map should be used?
questions.explanation: A political map shows how India is divided into states and union territories, matching this worksheet scenario.

questions.question: During a flood, rescue teams need to understand land and river paths quickly. Based on the worksheet scenario, which map type helps?
questions.explanation: A physical map helps rescue teams understand land and river paths, matching this worksheet scenario.

questions.question: The same real-world place can be shown very differently depending on which type of map (political, physical, or thematic) is used.
questions.explanation: Different map types highlight different information, so the same place can look very different depending on the map type used.

questions.question: Why might two people looking at maps of the same city see completely different information?
options: They might be looking at different types of maps (e.g. political vs. thematic)
Cities always look identical no matter the map type
Only one correct map of any city can ever exist
Maps of the same city are always drawn by the same person
questions.explanation: Different map types show different kinds of information, so two people could see very different things even for the same city.

questions.question: Which map type is best suited to show international or state boundaries?
questions.explanation: Political maps are best suited to show international or state boundaries.

questions.question: Which map type is best suited to show rivers, mountains, and valleys?
questions.explanation: Physical maps are best suited to show rivers, mountains, and valleys.

questions.question: Which map type is best suited to show one specific topic, like population density?
questions.explanation: A thematic map focuses on one topic, such as population density.

questions.question: Aarav, Meera, and a teacher each need a different map for different reasons. Whose need matches best with a physical map?
options: Meera, who is planning a trek through mountains
Aarav, who wants to know bordering states
The teacher, who wants to teach about states and union territories
None of them need a physical map
questions.explanation: Meera's need to learn about mountains and rivers for her trek matches best with a physical map.

questions.question: Whose need matches best with a political map — Aarav or the teacher?
questions.explanation: Both Aarav (bordering states) and the teacher (states/union territories) need a political map.

questions.question: Why does the chapter suggest we need MULTIPLE types of maps rather than just one 'all-purpose' map?
options: Because no single map can show every kind of information clearly at once
Because maps are expensive to print in more than one type
Because only one map type has ever existed
Because multiple maps make navigation harder
questions.explanation: Since no single map can clearly show every kind of information, we need multiple types of maps for different purposes.

questions.question: Give one real-life scenario where a thematic map would be essential.
options: Studying rainfall patterns across a region
Measuring temperature in a single room
questions.explanation: Studying rainfall patterns is a classic example of when a thematic map is essential.

questions.question: Give one real-life scenario where a physical map would be essential.
options: Planning a trek through mountains and rivers
Finding a country's political boundary only
questions.explanation: Planning a trek through mountains and rivers is a classic example of when a physical map is essential.

questions.question: Give one real-life scenario where a political map would be essential.
options: Understanding how a country is divided into states
questions.explanation: Understanding a country's division into states is a classic example of when a political map is essential.

questions.question: What is a cartographer?
options: A person who studies places carefully and draws maps
A person who only sells maps
A person who only reads maps
questions.explanation: A cartographer is a person who studies places carefully and draws maps of them.

questions.question: What must a cartographer do before drawing an accurate map?
options: Only copy other existing maps exactly
Avoid visiting or researching the place at all
questions.explanation: A cartographer must study a place carefully before they can draw an accurate map of it.

questions.question: In ancient India, which text described regions, routes, and boundaries useful for map-making?
questions.explanation: The Arthashastra, an ancient Indian text, described regions, routes, and boundaries useful for understanding territory.

questions.question: Why were maps important to rulers during the Mughal period?
options: They helped manage the empire, including taxes, city planning, and travel routes
Maps were only used for decoration in palaces
Maps had no real practical use for rulers
Maps were only used by foreign traders
questions.explanation: Mughal rulers used maps and land records to manage their empire, including for taxes, city planning, and travel routes.

questions.question: What did Mughal rulers use detailed maps and land records for?
options: Taxes, city planning, and travel routes
questions.explanation: Mughal rulers used detailed maps and land records for taxes, city planning, and travel routes.

questions.question: Which city is shown as the capital in BOTH the 1530 Mughal Empire map and the modern India map, according to the chapter?
questions.explanation: Delhi is shown as the capital in both the 1530 Mughal Empire map and the modern India map.

questions.question: The Mughal-era region called 'Malwa' lies in which present-day Indian state?
questions.explanation: The Mughal-era region of Malwa lies in present-day Madhya Pradesh.

questions.question: 'Baluchistan,' shown on the Mughal Empire map, is part of which present-day country?
questions.explanation: Baluchistan, shown on the Mughal Empire map, is part of present-day Pakistan.

questions.question: Sri Lanka was part of the Mughal Empire in 1530, according to the chapter's map comparison.
questions.explanation: Sri Lanka was NOT part of the Mughal Empire in 1530, according to the chapter's map comparison.

questions.question: Which Gujarat cities were shown as part of the Mughal Empire, according to the chapter?
questions.explanation: Ahmedabad and Junagadh, cities in present-day Gujarat, were shown as part of the Mughal Empire.

questions.question: Why is comparing an old historical map (like the Mughal Empire map) to a modern map useful?
options: It helps us see how regions, borders, and names have changed over time
It has no real educational value
It only helps us learn about ancient food habits
It proves that maps never change over time
questions.explanation: Comparing historical and modern maps helps us understand how regions, borders, and names have changed over time.

questions.question: Ancient India already had some form of map-making, even before modern tools existed.
questions.explanation: Ancient Indian texts like the Arthashastra describe regions, routes, and boundaries, showing early forms of map-making.

questions.question: What does the Arthashastra suggest about map-making in ancient India?
options: That rulers understood and described regions, routes, and boundaries even without modern tools
That maps did not exist in ancient India at all
That only foreign travelers made maps of India
That the Arthashastra has nothing to do with geography
questions.explanation: The Arthashastra's descriptions of regions, routes, and boundaries suggest rulers had an early understanding of geography and mapping.

questions.question: Baluchistan was shown as part of the Mughal Empire in 1530, but is part of Pakistan today. What does this tell us about maps over time?

questions.question: Why might comparing a Mughal Empire map with a modern GIS map show us both HOW maps have changed AND HOW India's regions have changed?
options: It reveals differences in mapping technology as well as differences in borders, names, and territories over time
It only shows differences in colours used on the maps
It proves that maps and regions never actually change
It has no educational value at all
questions.explanation: Comparing these very different types of maps reveals both how mapping technology has advanced and how India's regions and borders have changed historically.

questions.question: What is the key message of the 'Think Like a Geographer' reflection section?
options: A good geographer observes, compares, connects, and draws conclusions using multiple maps, not just one
A good geographer only needs to memorise map titles
A good geographer should avoid using more than one map
A good geographer only studies satellite maps
questions.explanation: The key message is that a good geographer observes, compares, connects, and draws conclusions using multiple maps rather than relying on just one.
